column4: pcrec_compile() takes a NUL-terminated const char *pattern and has no length parameter.
pcrec_compile signature is int pcrec_compile(const char *pattern, const pcrec_options *opt, pcrec_output *out, pcrec_error *err).
A raw 0x00 byte inside the intended pattern silently truncates the compile performed by pcrec_compile().
A 3-byte pattern "a\0b" compiles as the 1-byte pattern "a", and pcrec_compile() reports success for that shorter pattern.
The NUL truncation is documented, checkable behavior of the NUL-terminated entry point, not a defect pcrec intends to fix in this API shape.

Measured against libpcre2 10.46 (dlopen via tests/fuzz/pcre2_abi.h): PCRE2_ZERO_TERMINATED compile of the buffer {'a',0,'b'} yields a pattern matching only "a" (1-byte match at start of subject "a\0b").
Measured against libpcre2 10.46: compiling {'a',0,'b'} with explicit length=3 yields the real 3-byte pattern, matching the full subject "a\0b" with span [0,3).
The only way to avoid NUL truncation is for the caller to pass the pattern's true length, which PCRE2's API accepts and pcrec_compile() does not.
The NUL truncation is an API-surface gap relative to PCRE2's length-taking mode, not a semantics divergence between the two engines' NUL handling (PCRE2's sentinel mode fails identically).
rx_info.pattern_len reports the actual byte count pcrec_compile() saw and compiled (the truncated count), not the caller's intended count.
rx_info lives in the generated artifact; pcrec_compile() hands its caller C source text, not a struct.
At compile time the only way to read pattern_len is to string-search out.c_src for the emitted ".pattern_len = N," line.
Reading pattern_len as a value requires compiling and linking the artifact first.
A caller that knows the pattern's true length should test it before compiling; if strlen(pattern) != known_length the pattern contains a NUL and the caller refuses it itself.
The strlen pre-flight catches the truncation before it happens using only the standard library.
pattern_len remains the after-the-fact instrument for an artifact the caller already has.
Verified: compiling the byte-built 3-byte "a\0b" buffer through the real pcrec_compile() produces out.c_src containing ".pattern_len = 1,".
The CLI cannot carry a NUL through argv at all, so the NUL probe goes through the library pcrec_compile(), not the CLI.
The "a\0b" pattern_len probe is pinned as tests/cli/run_cli_tests.sh case16.
pattern_len is the source byte count, not the count of bytes the matcher walks (e.g. 'a\nb' is 4 source bytes and pattern_len = 4).
The pattern_len source-byte-count property is pinned structurally in tests/codegen/run_codegen_tests.sh.
A length-taking compile ((pattern, length) overload or equivalent that refuses a pattern whose declared extent it cannot verify) is not part of the pcrec_compile() contract.
CHECK: full length-taking compile support is scheduled with DD-3, tracked as docs/dev/known_issues.md K9, and is the natural trigger for customer V-A's (pattern, length) compatibility shim.
A caller with an untrusted or NUL-containing pattern source must run the strlen pre-flight itself; nothing in pcrec_compile()'s signature enforces it.
The section 8.0 sample compiles and runs as written: built with gcc -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wl,-dead_strip against lib/pcrec.h and libpcrec.a, run, and its matcher.c/matcher.h output compiled in turn.
Consumers should link with -Wl,-dead_strip (ld64) or -Wl,--gc-sections (GNU ld).
libpcrec.a is a static archive in which the .rxt-source-file support (the --source composer) is statically reachable from the ordinary compile path.
A consumer that never calls pcrec_compile_defs or pcrec_rxt_source_parse still pulls the composer's object files in unless the linker drops unreachable sections.

Measured (2026-09-17 code review, L6 1.3): the -dead_strip flag alone recovers 43,968 of the 44,448 bytes those objects add to a minimal consumer's __text, leaving 480 bytes and two symbols the composer's early-return path still reaches.
Omitting the dead-strip/gc-sections linker flag is not wrong, only larger than needed.
pcrec_default_options(&opt) is the mandatory first step before using a pcrec_options.
A zero-initialized pcrec_options has prefix == NULL and every compile fails with "invalid symbol prefix".
pcrec_options.header_name == NULL (the default) produces a self-contained .c; setting it (e.g. "matcher.h") also produces a header.
pcrec_compile() returns nonzero (-1) on failure and sets err.msg, err.pos (size_t) and err.input (PCREC_ERR_INPUT_PATTERN or PCREC_ERR_INPUT_TEMPLATE).
out.c_src and out.h_src are malloc'd, NUL-terminated C source owned by the caller, who must free them.
out.h_src is non-NULL exactly when opt.header_name was set.
pcrec_output_free(&out) frees both buffers and sets both fields to NULL.
pcrec_default_options() is mandatory; skipping it fails every compile.
A zeroed pcrec_options has prefix == NULL, and pcrec refuses a NULL prefix; pcrec_default_options is not a convenience over a working zero state.
Measured: a memset-zeroed options struct returns -1 with err.msg == "invalid symbol prefix (must be a C identifier, <= 60 chars)" for a pattern that compiles fine after pcrec_default_options().
pcrec_default_options() sets prefix = "rx", encoding = PCREC_ENC_BYTE and header_name = NULL, and zeroes everything else.
A caller overrides fields after calling pcrec_default_options(), never instead of it.
Re-measured: a default-initialized pcrec_options has prefix=rx, encoding=0 (PCREC_ENC_BYTE), header_name=NULL, flags=0, engine=0.
pcrec_output owns two heap buffers and the caller frees them.
pcrec_output is a struct { char *c_src; char *h_src; }.
pcrec_output.c_src is malloc'd and freed with pcrec_output_free.
pcrec_output.h_src is malloc'd, or NULL when options.header_name == NULL.
pcrec_output_free() frees both buffers and NULLs both fields (measured before and after).
pcrec_output_free() is safe to call twice and safe on a struct whose h_src was never produced.
pcrec_output_free() is the only way to release the pcrec_output buffers.
Section 5.2's "no allocation, no lifecycle to manage" statement covers the MATCH path only; the compile path allocates and pcrec_output_free is its lifecycle.
h_src is non-NULL exactly when header_name was set (measured both ways); a caller should test h_src rather than header_name.
pcrec_compile() returns 0 on success and -1 on failure; a caller checks the return value, not the error struct.
pcrec_compile() fills err only on failure.
pcrec_compile() never abort()s the caller on the compile path.
Every allocation site on the compile path routes failure through the internal pcrec_ctx_nomem() and comes back as a normal -1-with-diagnostic return.
A caller that sets a memory limit to survive a hostile pattern does survive it: allocation failure yields -1 with a diagnostic, not an abort.
One abort() remains in the code deliberately, off the compile path: the syntax-dump path's detached string buffers, which run outside a compile and have no pcrec_error to report through.
DFA structural invariants refuse through pcrec_ctx_fail like every other "cannot happen" site in the compiler (K61); they no longer abort.
As of 2026-09-18 the never-abort/never-silently-succeed-under-OOM promise of pcrec_compile() has no exceptions.

When a pattern needs more than one internal attempt (the [ART-SIZE] size-term ladder, a --engine=auto DFA-overflow retry, or a size-cap retry rung), an allocation failure on a non-final attempt makes pcrec_compile() return -1 with a diagnostic rather than success from a fallback attempt (K60, D109).
The multi-attempt-ladder allocation-failure population was 2 of 3,159 corpus patterns at default axes (docs/dev/k60_measurement.md section 3).
make alloc's W4 witness: 108 of 158 forced failures were absorbed before the D109 fix, 0 after.
Allocation failure in the emitted DFA state legend's scratch buffers is an ordinary -1-with-diagnostic refusal; it no longer drops the legend and lets the compile succeed (K60, D105).
The state-legend scratch buffer is a fixed local and the remaining legend scratch lives in the compile's arena.
make alloc's W1 and W3 witnesses: 15 and 25 forced failures absorbed before the D105 fix, 0 after.
A compile that would previously have emitted a legend-less artifact under OOM now returns -1 with a diagnostic.
The emitted bytes of a compile that does not run out of memory are unchanged by the legend fix, so D105 is not an abi event.
A pattern can be REFUSED for compile-side resource reasons, a failure class distinct from a syntax error.
A resource refusal arrives through the same -1 return and the same pcrec_error as a syntax error; a caller distinguishes them by reading err.msg, not the return value.

Measured at the D56 boundary: pattern a{9795} compiles; a{9796} returns -1 with err.msg == "pattern too complex for the DFA engine (subset construction exceeds 48000000 state-set elements; try --engine=vm)".
A pattern refused for resource reasons is legal PCRE; the refusal is that compiling it would cost more than pcrec is willing to spend, so a caller reporting every -1 as bad regex syntax is wrong.
Measured: the same a{9796} compiles cleanly under --engine=vm, because that mode never builds the DFA whose cap the refusal names.
The escape named by the DFA-complexity diagnostic (--engine=vm) is real.
Two encodings compile: byte (the default) and utf8.
Under utf8 a character is one to four bytes and "." and a class match a whole character.
Under utf8 an ill-formed byte sequence in the SUBJECT matches nothing, with no validation pass and no error return.
Under utf8 a startpos passed to <prefix>_search must be a character boundary of the encoding.
<prefix>_next_pos (section 3.1.1) is the supported way to produce a character-boundary startpos, and the section 3.1 find-all loop uses it.

CHECK: the pcrec_options block quotes "all nineteen members" but lists twenty (prefix, encoding, flags, header_name, engine, step_budget, work_budget, unroll_k, vm_entry_shape, frame_capacity, six max_*, warn_emit_bytes, name, tune, features).
Every member of lib/pcrec.h's pcrec_options appears in the spec's quoted block with a one-line gloss; the full text per member is the header comment and, for a tuning axis, tuning.md section 2.
pcrec_options.prefix is a const char * C identifier prefix; default "rx".
pcrec_options.encoding is an int holding a PCREC_ENC_* value, per compile call.
pcrec_options.flags is a uint64_t carrying PCREC_CASELESS, PCREC_EMIT_MAIN, PCREC_NO_CAPTURES, PCREC_TRACE and the optimization-axis deny/force bits (catalogue in tuning.md section 2).
pcrec_options.header_name is a const char *; NULL means a self-contained .c.
pcrec_options.engine is an int taking PCREC_ENGINE_AUTO, PCREC_ENGINE_DFA or PCREC_ENGINE_VM.
pcrec_options.step_budget is an int64_t taking PCREC_STEP_BUDGET_DEFAULT, PCREC_STEP_BUDGET_NONE, or a count.
pcrec_options.work_budget is an int64_t taking PCREC_WORK_BUDGET_DEFAULT, PCREC_WORK_BUDGET_NONE, or a count.
pcrec_options.unroll_k is an int; PCREC_UNROLL_K_DEFAULT (0) means the built-in default.
pcrec_options.vm_entry_shape is an int taking PCREC_VM_ENTRY_AUTO (0), _PLAIN, _SHARED, _FORWARD or _INLINE; it is an ordinal rung, not a bit (tuning.md section 2.21).
pcrec_options.frame_capacity is an int; 0 means let the compiler size it.
pcrec_options.frame_capacity's 0 sentinel differs from rx_info's field of the same name, which uses -1 for unbounded.
pcrec_options.max_emit_code_bytes is a uint64_t RAISE-ONLY cap override; 0 means built-in.
pcrec_options.max_emit_bytes is a uint64_t RAISE-ONLY cap override; 0 means built-in.
pcrec_options.max_nfa_states is a uint64_t RAISE-ONLY compile budget; 0 means built-in.
pcrec_options.max_dfa_states_goto is a uint64_t RAISE-ONLY compile budget; 0 means built-in.
pcrec_options.max_subset_elems is a uint64_t RAISE-ONLY compile budget; 0 means built-in.
pcrec_options.max_auto_dfa_elems is a uint64_t RAISE-ONLY budget that governs the AUTO route's DFA attempt only; 0 means built-in.
pcrec_options.warn_emit_bytes is a uint64_t ADVISORY stderr-warning threshold, never a refusal; 0 DISABLES the warning.
pcrec_options.warn_emit_bytes can be lowered, unlike the max_* caps.
pcrec_options.name is a const char * giving what rx_info.name reports; NULL means use the prefix.
pcrec_options.tune is an int from PCREC_TUNE_MIN_SIZE to PCREC_TUNE_MAX_SPEED, range -2..+2; 0 is balanced and a structural no-op.
pcrec_options.features is a const char * naming the enabled feature-module set for this call, same vocabulary as --features; NULL means no request.
The six max_* members of pcrec_options are RAISE-ONLY.
A max_* value BELOW the built-in default is refused as a malformed option rather than honoured, so no caller can use one to manufacture someone else's refusal.
warn_emit_bytes is deliberately not raise-only because it never refuses anything, so lowering it cannot break a build.
docs/spec/limits.md is the home of the six max_* budgets; per-field derivations are lib/pcrec.h's comments.
pcrec_options.features is applied PER pcrec_compile() call.
pcrec_options.features accepts a comma-separated module-name list spelled as pcrec --list-syntax's module column spells them, the frozen named set "std1" (D37), "all", or "none".
An unknown name in pcrec_options.features is refused by name, as the CLI --features rule does, surfaced through pcrec_error like any compile-time refusal.
The pcrec_error wording for an unknown features name is identical to the CLI's "--features: <text>" stderr line minus the "--features: " prefix.
pcrec_options.features == NULL means "make no request" and is deliberately NOT the CLI's bare-invocation default (std1).
A library caller who never sets pcrec_options.features gets the raw, ungated compile with no module enabled.
A library caller wanting the CLI's bare-invocation behaviour passes "std1" or the exported constant pcrec_default_features explicitly.
The CLI always resolves a concrete value for pcrec_options.features (features ? features : pcrec_default_features) and never leaves it NULL, so a bare pcrec 'PATTERN' invocation is unaffected.
Applying pcrec_options.features touches no shared state (D19): two concurrent pcrec_compile() calls with different features values cannot race.
Each pcrec_compile() call resolves its features request into that compile's own internal state, never a process-global.
The CLI's own --features additionally installs a process-global read by --probe-ask, --count-groups and --list-source; pcrec_options.features affects only the one pcrec_compile() call.
pcrec_options.encoding is a per-compile-call scalar: one encoding per pcrec_compile() call, carried in this field and nowhere else.
There is no process-global, file-global or environment-variable encoding setting.
Mixing encodings inside one compilation unit or one binary is supported: each artifact is self-contained, carries its own prefix, and embeds exactly one encoding's residual block (section 3.1.1).
The CLI spells the encoding option -e NAME or --encoding=NAME.
PCREC_ENC_BYTE (0, the default) and PCREC_ENC_UTF8 (1) both compile.
The pcrec_options.encoding value is what rx_info.encoding reports (section 6).
Any other pcrec_options.encoding value is refused with "unknown encoding (want byte, utf8)", an ordinary -1-with-diagnostic return that writes no C.
A code point above 0xFF written as \x{...} is a compile error under the byte encoding and compiles under utf8.
The encoding reaches the parser only through a range check on a written \x{...} value (utf8_design.md section 2.7.3).
PCREC_ENC_ASCII no longer exists; PCREC_ENC_BYTE replaced it as a RENAME, not an alias.
CLI value "-e ascii" is now an unknown encoding.
The byte encoding treats every byte as a character, 0x80-and-up included, with no case and no meaning attached.

Every boolean option (PCREC_CASELESS, PCREC_EMIT_MAIN, PCREC_NO_CAPTURES, PCREC_UCP, strategy-denial/force flags) is one representation end-to-end: the same bit set by a CLI flag, carried in pcrec_options.flags, and reflected verbatim in rx_info.flags.
A boolean option bit is reflected verbatim in rx_info.flags except where deliberately masked (section 6.3).
PCREC_NO_CAPTURES recovers the pure-DFA artifact (<PREFIX>_NCAPS 1); captures are on by default.
PCREC_UCP is bit 34 of pcrec_options.flags.
PCREC_UCP carries PCRE2_UCP's semantics (docs/spec/cli.md --ucp).
PCREC_UCP changes answers, so it is NOT masked: rx_info.flags of an artifact compiled with --ucp has bit 34 set.
A pattern that turns UCP on inside itself with (*UCP) does not set PCREC_UCP bit 34, just as an inline (?i) does not set PCREC_CASELESS.
The pattern text, recorded in rx_info.pattern, is where inline (*UCP) is recorded.
CHECK: the arrival of the PCREC_UCP bit moved no emitted byte of any artifact compiled without it (no abi event).
A caller that round-trips its own flags through rx_info.flags will legitimately find some bits missing.
The bits masked out of rx_info.flags are the testing/tuning axes that change no answer (section 6.3).
docs/spec/tuning.md section 2 is the catalogue of axes (bit, CLI spelling, what it denies or forces, why it is masked) and section 4 maps every bit to its pcrec_options field.
The spec tier is the contract (D80); lib/pcrec.h's comments are the implementation's record of the same facts, not their authority.
pcrec_error carries which input a diagnostic's pos indexes into.
pcrec_err_input is an enum with PCREC_ERR_INPUT_PATTERN = 0 and PCREC_ERR_INPUT_TEMPLATE = 1.
pcrec_error has member char msg[256].
pcrec_error has member size_t pos.
pcrec_error has member pcrec_err_input input.
pcrec_compile() always sets err.input = PCREC_ERR_INPUT_PATTERN today; it has no other input yet.
PCREC_ERR_INPUT_TEMPLATE has no producer yet; a future substitution-template compiler is its first producer.
pcrec_compile() returns 0 on success (out filled) or -1 on failure (err filled if non-NULL).
Verified: the unterminated group "a(b" returns -1 with err.pos == 1 and err.input == PCREC_ERR_INPUT_PATTERN.
PCREC_* names only pcrec's own enum/bit-valued constants, never a struct field name and never a bare CLI flag spelling.
The one exception to PCREC_* naming is the per-artifact PCREC_FEATURE_SET and PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES stamps, which carry the PCREC_* spelling without living in lib/pcrec.h.
The list of PCREC_*-named things outside lib/pcrec.h is exhaustive: it has exactly the two feature stamps.
The exported feature-default data symbol (src/parse/enabled.c, D37's bare-default mapping point) is the lower-case pcrec_default_features.
PCRE2_* spellings are reserved for a future PCRE2-compatibility layer and are never native to pcrec.
docs/spec/match_api.md records what shipped and is pcrec's contract with an embedder; design records (match_api_m4.md, engine_m4.md) record why.
Pre-v1 posture (D40): the contract carries no backwards-compatibility weight yet.
Pre-v1, breaking changes are unconstrained in substance and governed only in form: one announced-boundary commit per break, populations conserved and accounted, never silent drift.
At a future v1 declaration this document (or its direct successor) becomes the compatibility-bound enumeration.
Until v1, "frozen" in this spec means "the M4 working baseline", not "permanent".
Every artifact pcrec emits exports <prefix>_search_in, <prefix>_match_in and <prefix>_match_caps_in.
Every artifact declares the <prefix>_buffers descriptor, carries the five sizing macros in its header and the four sizing fields on rx_info.
The caller-provided-buffer surface exists on both engines and is present and inert on a DFA artifact.
A generated matcher never allocates (section 5.2).
The resume stack and its undo trail are sized at compile time and live in the entry point's own stack frame.
The artifact's depth ceiling is a compile-time constant by default.
Per D71 item 2 a caller may supply the backtracking storage instead, keeping pcrec's never-allocates property while lifting the depth ceiling as far as the caller reserves.
Measured on a default -p rx --features all build of ^(a(?1)?b)$ (recursion depth grows with the subject): it matches up to a 684-byte subject and returns PCREC_ERR_FRAMES at a 686-byte one.
The default depth ceiling is expressed as a subject size, not a fixed number.
libpcre2 10.46 matches 800 KB of the same ^(a(?1)?b)$ shape (cited from subroutines_design.md section 5.6, not measured in this doc).
Measured: on the left-recursive runaway ^(a|(?1)a)$ over a^n b, PCREC_ERR_FRAMES is returned in 0.0006 s at every n from 100 to 100,000, flat across a 1,000x range.
libpcre2's cost on that runaway grows as the square of the subject (2.6-5.6 s at n = 20,000; exponent 2.04), cited from subroutines_design.md section 5.6.
The default artifact refuses a legitimate deep match as the price of refusing a runaway in constant time; section 10.6 is how a caller buys the depth back.
<prefix>_buffers is a typedef'd struct with members void *frames, size_t nframes, void *trail, size_t ntrail.
<prefix>_buffers.frames is storage for resume frames.
<prefix>_buffers.nframes is the capacity in frames, not bytes.
<prefix>_buffers.trail is storage for trail entries.
<prefix>_buffers.ntrail is the capacity in entries, not bytes.
int <prefix>_search_in(const unsigned char *s, size_t n, size_t startpos, ptrdiff_t (*caps)[2], const <prefix>_buffers *buf).
ptrdiff_t <prefix>_match_in(const rx_ctx *ctx, const <prefix>_buffers *buf).
ptrdiff_t <prefix>_match_caps_in(const rx_ctx *ctx, ptrdiff_t (*caps_out)[2], const <prefix>_buffers *buf).
Each _in entry equals its un-suffixed sibling in anchoring promise, return space, caps/caps_out discipline and give-up codes, plus one argument naming where the working storage lives.
Sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 4 and 5 apply to the _in entries unchanged.
<prefix>_buffers is PER-ARTIFACT, scoped by --prefix; it is not one of section 1's fixed-literal rx_* ABI types.
A resume frame's size differs between artifacts, so the buffer type is per-artifact; a fixed-literal spelling would advertise an interchangeability that does not exist.
Measured: a resume frame is 24 bytes on an artifact with no LINKED call and 40 bytes on one with a linked call (RX_VM_CALL_LINKED > 0).
A call that wave G SPLICED (RX_VM_CALL_SPLICED) is inlined and adds nothing to the resume frame.
Measured: the email specimen's factored form under --engine=vm stamps a 24-byte frame with ten spliced calls.
A caller reads the frame-size stamp and never infers it from the pattern text.
The nframes and ntrail counts are CAPACITIES (frames / trail entries), not byte sizes; section 10.4 is how a caller converts bytes to counts.
frames and trail are two separate regions and BOTH are required when buf is non-NULL; supplying one without the other is not expressible.
Measured on ^(a(?1)?b)$: the trail is the array that binds first at the stamped defaults, so raising only nframes would produce no change.
buf == NULL is defined to be exactly a call to the un-suffixed entry with the same other arguments, and an artifact is free to implement it as one.
A give-up from an _in entry means the buffer in use ran out, and the code does not say whose buffer it was.
PCREC_ERR_FRAMES is returned for a caller-supplied buffer exactly as for the stamped default, naming a RESOURCE rather than an array or owner (section 4).
The count of frames or trail entries that WOULD have sufficed is NOT reported on a give-up.
Reporting the sufficient count requires the diagnostic axis; the default artifact does not carry the machinery (D71 item 1 treatment).
A give-up is RETRYABLE: calling the same entry again with the same subject and startpos and a larger buffer is defined.

The matcher holds no state between calls (section 5.3), the caller's caps array is untouched on every negative return, and the buffers are pure scratch, so give-up/double/retry is a correct algorithm.
The contents of a caller-supplied buffer after any call are UNSPECIFIED; a caller must not read them and need not re-initialise them before the next call.
Both buffer regions must be suitably aligned for the artifact's own frame and trail types; <PREFIX>_BUFFER_ALIGN states the requirement.
Storage from malloc, mmap, or a declaration of any ordinary object type satisfies the alignment requirement on every target pcrec supports.
<PREFIX>_BUFFER_ALIGN exists for a caller doing pointer arithmetic inside a larger arena.
The frame and trail layouts are private to the artifact, are not published, and a caller must not assume them.
The emitted header carries five sizing macros: <PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES, _TRAIL_FRAMES, _RESUME_FRAME_SIZE, _TRAIL_FRAME_SIZE, _BUFFER_ALIGN.
<PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES is the stamped DEFAULT resume-frame capacity (example value 2048).
<PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAMES is the stamped default trail capacity (example value 3072).
<PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAME_SIZE is the bytes per resume frame for THIS artifact (example value 40).
<PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAME_SIZE is the bytes per trail entry (example value 16).
<PREFIX>_BUFFER_ALIGN is the required buffer alignment (example value 8).
The sizing macro values are stamped for the target and are not constants of pcrec; a reader must not take 40 as one.
Measured: a resume frame is 24 bytes on a call-free artifact, 40 on a call-bearing one, and 32 and 48 on the --trace versions of the same two.
A resume frame's size also depends on the target's own type sizes.
pcrec computes each sizing number at compile time from the same member list that emits the frame struct, so the two cannot drift.
The artifact asserts each stamped sizing macro against the real sizeof/_Alignof at its own build, so a number computed for a different target model is a loud compile error naming the macro.
A caller reads the sizing macros and never hardcodes their values.
CHECK: the two capacity macros (<PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES, <PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAMES) are in the generated .h where a caller can read them (they previously lived in the generated .c).
rx_info carries four of the same sizing facts for a consumer with no C header (an FFI or dlopen binding).
rx_info.resume_frames is an int64_t giving the stamped default capacity.
rx_info.trail_frames is an int64_t.
rx_info.resume_frame_size is an int32_t giving bytes per resume frame.
rx_info.trail_frame_size is an int32_t giving bytes per trail entry.
CHECK: rx_info.abi is the layout version and is bumped on every layout change (section 6 rule "layout version; bump-on-change").
rx_info.resume_frames duplicates frame_capacity's information for the bounded case but is not redundant with it.
rx_info.frame_capacity reports -1 for "no bound at all" on a DFA artifact and answers a different question than resume_frames (section 6 sentinel-asymmetry note).
A stamped size of 0 means "this engine takes no buffers"; every DFA artifact stamps 0 because it has no resume stack.
Dividing bytes by <PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAME_SIZE is a division by zero on any DFA artifact.
A stamped 0 is rx_info's honest signal; pcrec does not stamp a fake non-zero size for storage that is never read.
A caller must test the stamped size before dividing by it and pass NULL when it is 0.
An _in entry on an artifact with stamped size 0 accepts a descriptor and ignores it, so NULL and a correctly-sized buffer are the same call there.
On a DFA artifact the whole buffer surface is present and inert, so a caller can write one call site against both engines.
The three _in entries, the <prefix>_buffers type and all five sizing macros are emitted on EVERY artifact.
On a DFA artifact the four sizing macros and the four rx_info sizing fields read 0.
On a DFA artifact an _in entry accepts a descriptor and ignores it, answering exactly as its un-suffixed sibling does.

The five buffer sizing macros are a deliberate departure from section 6.3's rule that per-artifact budget/capacity macros are VM-artifacts-only, because they are what a caller needs to CALL the artifact rather than what the artifact DID.
Section 5.3's concurrency rule gains one conjunct: concurrent calls need each their own caps/caps_out buffer AND their own frame and trail buffers.
Two concurrent calls sharing one <prefix>_buffers region are a data race in the CALLER's code, and the matcher does not serialize it.
One thread re-entering a matcher from a callout needs its own storage for the inner call.
There is deliberately no way to set a buffer once per artifact or per thread; the buffer travels with the call.
Emitted code has no mutable state (section 5.3, checked by TS-1) and no thread-local buffer, since a thread-local would fail reentrancy.
The operating system materialises only the pages the match actually touches in a lazily-committed reservation.

On an artifact whose stamped default storage does not fit inside one 4 KB page, each un-suffixed entry first runs the match on a page-budgeted buffer of <PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES / <PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL (section 6.3).
On PCREC_ERR_FRAMES and on no other outcome, the tiered un-suffixed entry re-runs the same match from scratch on the full stamped default and returns the second run's result.
Every other first-run outcome (match, no-match, PCREC_ERR_STEPS, _WORK, _RECURSE, PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL) is returned directly from the fast tier.
A FRAMES escalation restarts the step and work budgets: they are per CALL, not per tier, and the second run begins with both full.
Because of the budget restart, one call may spend up to twice each budget (stated in section 4).
The wasted fast attempt is bounded by the step and work budgets, not by the fast frame count.

Tiering changes no answer: the deep run is a bit-for-bit replay of a single-tier entry from scratch (same capacities, both budgets refilled, same start-position loop over the same prefilter, one deterministic engine).
Nothing the fast attempt did carries into the deep run: run state is a local of the tier that declared it, with no allocation, no thread-local and no mutable static (section 5.3).
For every artifact, subject and entry, the returned value and written capture spans are those the entry produced before the tier existed.

The fast attempt may reach PCREC_ERR_FRAMES where a single-tier run would have reached PCREC_ERR_STEPS; that FRAMES value is never returned (it is the escalation trigger) and the replay then reports PCREC_ERR_STEPS.

The four [ART-SIZE] size-term macros follow the <PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN precedent: a selection fact stamped whether or not it fired (D81).
<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K and <PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY are VM-artifact-scoped because a DFA artifact has no counter rung to have chosen a K for.
<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K is the unroll factor this artifact was emitted at.
<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY takes SEVEN values, because "the term did not run" has several distinguishable reasons a check must tell apart.
<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY == "option" means an explicit --unroll=K.
<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY == "denied" means -fno-size-term.
<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY == "default" means the term ran and the artifact was below its threshold.
<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY == "size-model" means the ladder ran and its K was taken.
<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY == "size-model-declined" means the ladder ran and the materiality bar rejected its K.
<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY == "cap-rescue" means the bar declined a K and an emitted-size cap took it anyway.

<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY == "capacity-declined" means the ladder ran and the K it wanted would have LOWERED the artifact's declared capacity (.frame_capacity or .subject_ceiling) below what the default K declares, so it was not a candidate (limits.md section 8a).
